overall: Atlanta is sitting at a warm and humid 77.0°F overnight low as of 05:30 ET, with dewpoints in the 71–73°F range indicating deep tropical moisture in place. Temperatures have been completely flat all night with zero velocity, which is typical of a moist, cloudy overnight profile — the broken cloud deck (62% coverage, low ceiling ~488m) has suppressed radiative cooling. The setup favors a warm afternoon but cloud cover and convective potential from the high moisture load introduce some uncertainty in the peak.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are in moderate agreement on a warm day, ranging from NBM at 81.9°F to HRRR at 86.2°F and ECMWF at 83.7°F — a roughly 4-degree spread. The HRRR's higher projection likely reflects its better convective-scale resolution of the boundary layer heating potential, while NBM is the conservative anchor. The intraday model skews warmer (86–91°F range) given the very high overnight running minimum, while the META model peaks cleanly at 86–87°F (29.7%).
max_temp_prediction: The weight of evidence points to a daily high in the mid-80s, most likely near 86°F. The META model's dominant bucket at 86–87°F (29.7%), combined with NWP model clustering in the 82–86°F range and the anomalously warm overnight low of 77°F, supports this estimate. Confidence is moderate — the high dewpoints and broken clouds could either constrain afternoon heating or fuel afternoon thunderstorm activity that caps the high, but the warm air mass in place makes it difficult to stay much below 84°F.
